title: Kebab barg
subtitle: Persian grilled lamb fillet with saffron
excerpt: Kebab barg is one of the great Persian grilled meats: thin slices of lamb fillet marinated in saffron, onion, and lime, then grilled quickly over high heat until just charred on the edges. It is served over saffron rice with a grilled tomato, raw onion, and a knob of butter.
sourceNotes: One of the premium kebabs served in Persian restaurants. Barg means leaf, referring to the thin, flat cuts of lamb that are characteristic of this dish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the lamb for 4 to 24 hours in the fridge. Grill just before serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: Grill or griddle at maximum heat for best char

content.text: Kebab barg is the kebab that turns up on special occasions and in the better Persian restaurants. The lamb is cut thin, no thicker than a finger, and marinated in saffron and onion until the meat is deeply fragrant. Grilled over high heat for just a few minutes, the edges char slightly while the centre stays tender.

The key is the quality of the lamb and the heat of the grill. The grill must be very hot before the meat goes on, and the pieces should cook fast. Long, slow cooking would make the thin lamb dry and tough.
In Iran, kebab barg is grilled over charcoal, which adds a smokiness that a griddle pan cannot fully replicate. A very hot griddle pan still produces a good result.

items.prepNote: cut across the grain into 1 cm thick slices
generous pinch, steeped in 3 tbsp hot water

content.text: Combine the grated onion, saffron water, olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Add the lamb slices and turn to coat well. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.

Heat a griddle pan over the highest heat until smoking hot. Pat the lamb pieces dry with kitchen paper (wet lamb steams rather than chars). Grill in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side until charred at the edges and just cooked through. Remove and rest for 2 minutes. Grill the whole tomatoes alongside for 5 minutes until soft and lightly charred.
Lay the kebab pieces over saffron rice. Place a knob of butter on the hot lamb so it melts over the rice. Serve with grilled tomatoes, raw sliced onion, and flatbread.

rows.fix: Use leg or fillet, sliced thin and cooked quickly. Any longer than 3 minutes per side on a thin slice is too long.

rows.cause: Pan not hot enough or lamb too wet
rows.fix: Pat the lamb dry before grilling. A very hot dry pan is essential for colour.

rows.cause: Too little saffron or not steeped properly
rows.fix: Use a good pinch of saffron and steep in very hot water for at least 10 minutes before using in the marinade.

content.text: Kebab barg can also be made with chicken breast pounded thin. Add a little sumac to the raw onion served alongside; it is the traditional Persian accompaniment. If cooking outdoors on a barbecue, thread the lamb pieces on flat metal skewers.
The lamb can marinate for up to 24 hours in the fridge. Do not grill until just before eating; the charred edges do not hold well and the lamb is much better freshly cooked.

Kebab barg is sold in Persian restaurants in Iran and in the diaspora. It is considered a premium kebab, often priced above koobideh and other minced kebabs on the menu. It appears at celebrations and family gatherings and is the kind of dish people choose when they want the best.
